stem.text: The Boltzmann distribution is shown for a sample of gas at an initial temperature, $T_{1}$.

stem.alt: Boltzmann distribution curve labelled T1: proportion of molecules with energy E against molecular energy E, single peak at low energy with a long tail.

stem.text: The sample of gas was heated to temperature, $T_{2}$.
What is the correct distribution for the higher temperature, $T_{2}$?

A.alt: Curve labelled T2 that looks almost identical to the T1 curve.

B.alt: Curve labelled T2 with a low, very broad peak at moderate energy and a long tail.

C.alt: Curve labelled T2 with a peak lower than the T1 peak and shifted to higher energy.

D.alt: Curve labelled T2 with a tall, narrow peak at low energy and a flat tail close to zero.
